reason: The README documents the aig-infra-scan CLI, a Go fingerprint/vulnerability scanner that runs offline on CPU with no API key.
goal: Get the AI-Infra-Guard infrastructure scanner CLI (aig-infra-scan from infra-scan/, or the Go CLI built from cmd/cli) working so that `aig-infra-scan -t http://127.0.0.1:PORT --lang en --json -o result.json` scans a local HTTP service and reports the detected AI product. The command must be available on PATH (via /work/env.sh) and must use the bundled fingerprint rules from the repo's data/ directory. No LLM/API key is needed.
check: The hidden test starts a fake Ollama HTTP service locally, scans it with the CLI, and verifies the output identifies Ollama for that target.

revision.by: fairness review (every maintained-set exam re-checked against the source)
issues: Too lenient: the JSON report includes the raw HTTP response as a field named "Resp", so `grep -qi ollama result.json` matches the fake service's body 'Ollama is running' even when no fingerprint rule fires (e.g. data/fingerprints not loaded). The goal's own requirement ('must use the bundled fingerprint rules') is therefore never tested.
Falling back to grepping stdout when result.json is empty is also lenient: USAGE.md says --json -o writes the report to the file.

v2 parses the JSON array and requires fingerprints[].name=='ollama', version '0.1.20' extracted from /api/version, and at least one advisory (data/vuln_en/ollama has rules such as version <= "0.3.14").
The fixed `sleep 2` before scanning is replaced by a readiness poll.
evidence: src/tencent-ai-infra-guard/common/runner/result.go:38-47 — HttpResult has `Resp string` with no json tag, so it is emitted as "Resp"
src/tencent-ai-infra-guard/common/runner/runner.go:346-357 — Resp: resp.DataStr is set for every target, fingerprinted or not; :563-568 — --json writes the ResultsJSON array to the -o file
src/tencent-ai-infra-guard/data/fingerprints/ollama.yaml — body matcher 'Ollama is running' and a version extractor on /api/version
oracles/tencent-ai-infra-guard.sh:36 — grep -qi ollama on the file
